note: NEW ARM, not the generator: HYBRID = the Haiku builder writes the page by hand, exactly like the baseline (own layout, own illustrations; the engine's page generators build_site/compose_page/suggest_layout/brief_template are forbidden), but ALSO has the engine's QA tools (validate_design, detect_ai_slop, analyze_visual_quality, capture_preview, search_icons, generate_design_system) and is required to run validate_design and detect_ai_slop on its page, read the findings and fix them. In this release's data files the hybrid arm is stored under the label 'engine' (so existing scripts work); in the tables below the 'engine' columns ARE the hybrid arm. Four never-seen domains (tidewater marina, ironbark bookshop, loomhouse weaving studio, quartermaster restaurant inventory SaaS), fresh agents for both arms, engine frozen for the run (the CTA false-positive fix in verify was applied BEFORE the evaluation so both arms are scored by the same gate; audit numbers are not strictly comparable to earlier releases). CONFOUNDS, important: (1) the hybrid prompt tells the agent to 'make your own design decisions, your own layout, your own illustrations', wording the baseline prompt lacks - part of the originality gain may be this instruction and not the tools; (2) the hybrid arm did more iteration (18-29 tool calls vs 14-24 and about 8% more tokens): the gain could come from any extra critique loop rather than from the engine tools specifically; a control arm (baseline + the 'make your own design decisions' sentence + a generic self-review loop with no engine tools) is NOT yet run, so the result shows hybrid beats baseline but NOT that the engine tools are the cause; (3) n = 4 briefs x 2 label orders, one build per brief and arm, Sonnet judges judging Haiku from screenshots; (4) one hybrid agent made a stray, out-of-scope call to a remote-session creation tool, which the permission system denied (nothing was created); (5) three hybrid agents left the engine's .openui/ preview folder inside site/ (excluded from measurements). The QA gate did catch real defects in hand-written pages that agents then fixed (console 404s, contrast failures, horizontal overflow, sub-12px text, a failing pricing-toggle interaction), and exposed a false positive in the gate itself (fixed).
